goals.goal: Build a working backend that supports recipe storage, ingredient matching, and cuisine fusion queries.
Keep it simple. No auth, no migrations, no ORM. This is an MVP for academic demonstration.
All routes return HTML snippets, not JSON. HTMX on the frontend will consume them.

constraints.constraint: Do NOT use SQLAlchemy or any ORM.
Do NOT use FTS5 virtual tables. Removed from scope.
Do NOT add security middleware, rate limiting, or input sanitization beyond basic SQL safety.
Every db connection must be opened and closed within the route function that uses it. No global connection objects.
Use render_template for full HTML files. Use render_template_string for inline HTML snippets returned by routes.

agent.name: DatabaseSchemaAgent
agent.responsibility: Create init_db.py. This script builds the schema and seeds the database. It runs once before the app starts.

instructions.step: Connect to flavorforge.db using sqlite3.connect("flavorforge.db"). Use a context manager (with statement) so the connection closes cleanly.
Execute CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for each table below, in this exact order to respect foreign key dependencies.

Insert exactly 3 cuisines using INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Cuisines (name) VALUES (?).
Italian Indian Mexican

Insert exactly 10 ingredients using INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Ingredients (name) VALUES (?).
tomato garlic onion chicken cumin cheese pasta chili olive oil garam masala
Insert exactly 5 recipes into the Recipes table. Capture the lastrowid for each insert to use in junction table seeding.

For each recipe seeded in step 1.5: - Look up ingredient ids from Ingredients table by name. - Insert into Recipe_Ingredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id) for each ingredient. - Look up cuisine id from Cuisines table by name. - Insert into Recipe_Cuisines (recipe_id, cuisine_id). Use INSERT OR IGNORE to avoid duplicate key errors on re-runs.
Call conn.commit() after all inserts. Print "Database initialized successfully." to stdout on completion.

validation.check: Running python init_db.py twice must not throw errors (IF NOT EXISTS and INSERT OR IGNORE handle idempotency).
flavorforge.db must exist after the script runs.
All 5 tables must exist with correct columns.
Recipes table must have 5 rows. Ingredients must have 10. Cuisines must have 3.
Recipe_Ingredients and Recipe_Cuisines must have the correct number of rows matching seed data.

agent.name: FlaskAppAgent
agent.responsibility: Create app.py. This is the Flask application with all four routes. Depends on Agent 1 having already created the database.

dependencies.dependency: flavorforge.db must exist before this app starts.

imports.import: from flask import Flask, request, render_template, render_template_string

agent.app_setup: Define app = Flask(__name__). Define a helper function get_db_connection() that returns a sqlite3.connect("flavorforge.db") connection with row_factory set to sqlite3.Row so columns are accessible by name.

route.logic: Return render_template("index.html"). No database call needed.

route.description: Adds a new recipe with ingredients and cuisine to the database.

logic.step: INSERT INTO Recipes (name, instructions) VALUES (recipe_name, '') and capture lastrowid as recipe_id.

For each ingredient in the ingredients list: - Strip whitespace. Skip if empty string. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Ingredients (name) VALUES (ingredient). - SELECT id FROM Ingredients WHERE name = ingredient to get ingredient_id. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Recipe_Ingredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id) VALUES (recipe_id, ingredient_id).

For the cuisine string: - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Cuisines (name) VALUES (cuisine). - SELECT id FROM Cuisines WHERE name = cuisine to get cuisine_id. - INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Recipe_Cuisines (recipe_id, cuisine_id) VALUES (recipe_id, cuisine_id).

route.returns: HTML snippet string using render_template_string. Format: a single table row. Example: {recipe_name}Added

route.description: Takes a list of ingredients the user has on hand. Returns recipes ranked by how many of those ingredients they contain.

logic.step: Clean the ingredients list: strip whitespace, filter empty strings, lowercase all values.

Build a parameterized SQL query. Use a placeholder string for the IN clause based on the length of the list. Example placeholder: (?, ?, ?) for 3 ingredients.
SQL pattern: SELECT r.name, COUNT(i.name) as match_count FROM Recipes r JOIN Recipe_Ingredients ri ON r.id = ri.recipe_id JOIN Ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.id WHERE LOWER(i.name) IN ({placeholders}) GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY match_count DESC

route.returns:
HTML snippet using render_template_string. An unordered list of results. Each list item shows recipe name and match count. Example:
  • Pasta Pomodoro — 3 ingredients matched
    • If no results:
  • No matching recipes found.

route.description: Takes two cuisine names. Returns recipes that belong to BOTH cuisines simultaneously. Uses a double-join with HAVING COUNT = 2 strategy.

logic.step:
SQL pattern: SELECT r.name FROM Recipes r JOIN Recipe_Cuisines rc ON r.id = rc.recipe_id JOIN Cuisines c ON rc.cuisine_id = c.id WHERE c.name IN (cuisine_a, cuisine_b) GROUP BY r.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = 2
Use parameterized query: WHERE c.name IN (?, ?) with (cuisine_a, cuisine_b) as params.

route.returns:
HTML snippet using render_template_string. A div with a heading and a list of recipe names. Example:
Fusion: Italian + Indian
  • Recipe Name
If no results:

No fusion recipes found for these two cuisines.

agent.app_runner: At the bottom of app.py, under if __name__ == "__main__": Call app.run(debug=True).

validation.check: python app.py must start without errors after init_db.py has been run.
POST /add_recipe with valid form data must return a table row HTML string and persist the recipe in the db.
POST /predictive_match with ingredients that exist in seed data must return at least one list item.
POST /cultural_fusion with cuisine_a=Italian and cuisine_b=Indian must return the fusion div (may be empty list if no cross-cuisine recipes in seed data — that is acceptable).
No route should crash on empty input. Handle empty lists gracefully.

agent.name: IntegrationValidationAgent
agent.responsibility: Verify the full backend pipeline works correctly before frontend work begins. This agent does not create files. It runs checks only.

dependencies.dependency: init_db.py must have been executed successfully.
app.py must be running on http://127.0.0.1:5000.

checks.check: Assert flavorforge.db exists in the project root.

Open flavorforge.db and verify: - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Recipes = 5 - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Ingredients = 10 - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Cuisines = 3 - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Recipe_Ingredients is greater than 0 - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Recipe_Cuisines is greater than 0
Send GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/ Assert HTTP 200 response.

Send POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/add_recipe with form data: - recipe_name = "Test Recipe" - ingredients[] = "tomato" - ingredients[] = "garlic" - cuisine = "Italian" Assert response contains "Test Recipe". Assert Recipes table now has 6 rows.

Send POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/predictive_match with form data: - ingredients[] = "tomato" - ingredients[] = "garlic" Assert response contains at least one <li> element. Assert response does not crash (HTTP 200).

Send POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/cultural_fusion with form data: - cuisine_a = "Italian" - cuisine_b = "Indian" Assert HTTP 200 response. Assert response contains either a recipe name or the no-results message. Neither outcome is a failure — empty fusion result is valid given seed data.
Send POST /predictive_match with an empty ingredients[] list. Assert HTTP 200 and no server crash. Send POST /add_recipe with empty recipe_name. Assert HTTP 200 and no server crash.

agent.pass_condition: All checks return HTTP 200. No 500 errors. Row counts match expected values. Backend is considered stable and ready for frontend integration.

execution_order.step: If all Agent 3 checks pass, backend phase is complete. Frontend phase begins in next prompt.
